page: Microsoft Azure F48alds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, delivering 48 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. Memory is configured at 96.0 GB total, establishing a low memory footprint of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators such as GPUs are not included, and complementary public IPv4 addresses are not provisioned by default.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate top-tier performance across raw processor metrics and I/O-intensive workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core scores reached 3,578.07 while multi-core scaled to 169,619.46, placing both in the top 10% tier. PassMark CPU tests recorded 96,241.45 overall and 119,656.78 in extended instructions, supported by AMD instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. Memory bandwidth achieved 9,203.3 GB/sec in cached 16 KB read tests and 290.23 GB/sec in large-block 256 MB reads. In-memory data workloads demonstrated significant throughput, generating 131.29 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a top-tier PassMark database operations score of 37,405.34.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio represents a hardware tradeoff favoring compute density and rapid local disk operations over large RAM allocations. While small and medium language model text processing reaches upper-quartile inference speeds, large 70B models exhibit average throughput (4.18 tokens/sec generation) due to the absence of dedicated GPUs and limited per-core memory capacity. Cost efficiency is optimized for parallelized, compute-heavy tasks that do not exceed 2 GB per core.

Microsoft Azure F48alds_v7 is suited for compute-bound workloads requiring fast local scratch space, including high-throughput web serving, continuous integration builds, batch data compression, and transactional database applications with constrained working memory footprints.
description: Microsoft Azure F48alds_v7 is a compute-optimized instance powered by a 48-core AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz with dedicated physical cores and no simultaneous multithreading. It features 96.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and integrates 5,670 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the server ranks in the top tier for multi-core compute, compression, and Redis operations, reaching 131.29 million SET operations per second and 169,619.46 in multi-core stress-ng tests. Memory throughput reaches 290.23 GB/sec on uncached reads. Given its 1:2 core-to-RAM ratio and dense local NVMe storage, the F48alds_v7 delivers strong performance-per-resource efficiency for high-performance computing, batch data processing, compiler tasks, and caching layers that operate within a 96 GB memory boundary.
